name: United States federal income tax
method: Annualized bracket withholding estimate. Taxable income is wages after pre-tax deductions that reduce federal income tax, plus W-4 Step 4a other income, minus the 2026 standard deduction and W-4 Step 4b deductions. Tax is computed from the Rev. Proc. 2025-32 rate schedules, then reduced by the W-4 Step 3 credit. If the Step 2 multiple-jobs checkbox is on, the estimate uses half the standard deduction and bracket thresholds at half width — an approximation of the Pub 15-T checkbox schedule, not the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator and not a payroll company's Pub 15-T table lookup.

sources.name: IRS newsroom, tax year 2026 inflation adjustments (Rev. Proc. 2025-32)
Tax Foundation, 2026 federal income tax brackets
IRS Publication 15-T, Federal Income Tax Withholding Methods

notes: Standard deduction: single and married filing separately $16,100; married filing jointly $32,200; head of household $24,150. Head of household bracket thresholds follow Rev. Proc. 2025-32 Table 2, including the 32% threshold at $201,750 and the 35% threshold at $256,200 (they are not identical to the single schedule). Supplemental wages are often withheld at a flat 22% federal rate; that method is offered on the bonus tool and is not the default paycheck math. Contribution limits are planning caps for warnings only: 401(k)/403(b)/TSP elective deferral $24,500; HSA $4,400 self-only and $8,750 family (Rev. Proc. 2025-19); health FSA salary reduction $3,400. Catch-up contributions are not applied automatically.
